technique.how: Inspect the skin around the knees after initial resuscitation. Score 0 = none; 1 = coin-sized area at centre of knee; 2 = not exceeding upper edge of kneecap; 3 = not exceeding middle thigh; 4 = not exceeding groin fold; 5 = beyond the groin fold. Reassess serially (e.g. 6-hourly).
technique.prerequisites: Adequate lighting, knees exposed; ideally scored after the initial resuscitation window.

interpretation.positive_finding: Mottling score 2-3 or 4-5 at 6 h is strongly associated with 14-day death in septic shock (OR 16 and 74 vs score 0-1); each extra point roughly doubles the odds of death.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absent or minimal mottling (0-1) after resuscitation marks a lower-risk group, but does not exclude shock or hypoperfusion.
interpretation.pitfalls: It is a prognostic (mortality) marker, not a diagnostic test for a specific shock type; dark skin, peripheral vascular disease, hypothermia and vasopressor dosing can alter appearance. It is not a proportion-based sens/spec sign.
interpretation.changes_what: A rising or persistent score (>=2) should trigger escalation: reassess perfusion, lactate and urine output, and intensify resuscitation or ICU involvement; a falling score suggests response.

estimates.target_condition: 14-day mortality in septic shock (prognostic, not diagnostic)
estimates.population: Consecutive adult septic shock patients (n=60), scored 6 h after inclusion
estimates.quote: mottling score [score 0-1 OR 1; score 2-3 OR 16, 95% CI (4-81); score 4-5 OR 74, 95% CI (11-1,568), p < 0.0001]

estimates.target_condition: 14-day mortality in sepsis/septic shock (prognostic, not diagnostic)
estimates.population: Adults with sepsis or septic shock, development cohort n=259 (Paris) with Brazilian validation cohort
estimates.quote: Mottling score at H6, by point 2.26 [1.72-2.97] < 0.001

sources.citation: Ait-Oufella H, Lemoinne S, Boelle PY, et al. Mottling score predicts survival in septic shock. Intensive Care Med 2011;37:801-807.

Dumas G, Lavillegrand JR, Joffre J, et al. Mottling score is a strong predictor of 14-day mortality in septic patients whatever vasopressor doses and other tissue perfusion parameters. Crit Care 2019;23:211.
Coudroy R, Jamet A, Frat JP, et al. Incidence and impact of skin mottling over the knee and its duration on outcome in critically ill patients. Intensive Care Med 2015;41:452-459.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use the score to decide against escalation; a low score never excludes shock. Validated mainly in septic shock, less in cardiogenic or hemorrhagic shock.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Score >=2 persisting after resuscitation is a marker of high short-term mortality; escalate to ICU-level care.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Excellent agreement between independent observers, kappa 0.87 (95% CI 0.72-0.97) in Ait-Oufella 2011.

extraction_notes: The evidence is prognostic (odds ratios for 14-day mortality), not sensitivity/specificity for a diagnosis, so all sens/spec/LR fields are null and ORs are recorded in the quotes. Ait-Oufella OR from abstract; Dumas per-point OR read from Table 2 of the PMC open-access full text (development cohort, Model 1). Coudroy 2015 cited for the incidence (29% of all ICU admissions; 49% in septic shock) and in-ICU mortality association (aOR 3.29). Prevalence fields hold the 14-day mortality rate of each cohort. Validator flags these two entries as having no sens/spec/LR field; they are retained deliberately because the only quantitative evidence for this sign is odds ratios for mortality (quote+location given), and dropping them would misrepresent the sign as unquantified.
